_comment: Every column of GOLDEN_COLUMNS must appear in exactly one of enforced, known_gaps, not_comparable or unfilled. The test refuses a column nobody has decided about.
_catalogue_comment: The capture is the WHOLE Vetapet catalogue replayed under the vet contract, so most rows rightly dead-letter: the retail/non-vet sections' headings are not this contract's to claim (CONTRACT_REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING on cost/description dominates). The 574-row lane split is pinned in the quality report, and the sheet's vet SKUs are the assertion surface.
_parked_comment: TOP250 (Topizole Shampoo 250mL) is deliberately NOT in expected.csv. The catalogue prints it as two same-code rows — ORDER UNIT '1-10 bottles' at HK$82.0 and '11-20 bottles' at HK$78.0. The sheet's answer is right (base $82.00, tier 'buy 11-20 BOTTLES at HKD 78 per BOTTLE'), but no mechanism folds same-code quantity-band rows into base-plus-term yet: both rows become candidates and the deeper band supersedes, publishing $78.00 as the base cost. Parked rather than pinned-wrong; the contract's VETAPET_VET_QUANTITY_BAND_ROWS ambiguity carries the defect, and the review desk sees both band candidates in the meantime. Wound-care SKUs (500-00xx) print the same shape at 3/6/12 pcs.
_missing_comment: APQ-L, VANG5L and VANG-RCP never reach the export: their tables print prices under headings the contract cannot claim (Apoquel's 'PRICE PER ORDER QTY: 1-19' / '20 or above' ladder columns; the vaccine tables' layout), so the rows dead-letter under CONTRACT_REQUIRED_FIELD_MISSING. They stay in expected.csv as open sheet assertions and join covered_skus only when the contract learns those layouts.

known_gaps.brand: brand now reads the page's brand mark (page_brand — the zoetis/Dermoscent wordmark heading each page), which this hand-captured envelope predates, so every covered row is empty. Recapture the envelope with the updated prompt and the sheet's Zoetis/Dermoscent values become reachable — this gap failing to fail is the signal to move brand toward enforced
known_gaps.package_configuration: prints the declared 'unit' fallback; the packing text of these layouts is not parsed into count-and-noun form
known_gaps.order_multiple: not derived — the vet layouts declare no order-increment source, so the column is empty
known_gaps.catalogue_price_basis_uom: the AMOUNT is per order unit and basis_qty matches 11/11, but the uom label resolves to the declared 'unit' fallback wherever no ORDER UNIT column or readable slash-unit names the specific noun (sheet: BOX/BOTTLE/PACK)
known_gaps.sellable_uom: same 'unit' fallback as the price basis label
known_gaps.sellable_units_per_price_basis: not derived for the vet layouts
known_gaps.rrp: the vet tables print no RRP column, and the retail-style tables print 'Suggested Price', which is not a declared RRP alias — every covered row is empty
known_gaps.weight: the sheet hand-fills weights; the export derives grams only from mass measures in packing text, and these rows print volume, length or nothing
known_gaps.mbb_tier_1: three shapes, none reachable yet: page-banner promotions land in text_observations (21501 'Mix over $1000, 10% off'); free-goods remarks are captured as MBB text, not a structured tier (ROT 'buy 3, get 1 free'); and same-code quantity-band rows have no folding mechanism (TOP250, parked)

not_comparable.supplier: the sheet labels these rows 'C.Vetapet & Company'; the operations supplier record this contract binds (id 91) is named 'Vetapet Vet'. Same company, two registers — the export prints the record's name. (Supplier master also carries id 4 'C. Vetapet' and id 61 'C. Vetapet & Company / Alfamedic'.)
not_comparable.product_name: the sheet holds a human shorthand ('Revolution Pup and Kitten'); the export holds the supplier's printed description ('Revolution 15mg for Puppies & Kittens (Mauve 5 lbs or less)')
not_comparable.product name [Rosetta]: a hand-authored retail name, not something the pipeline derives
